title: Question Mark Above Line

illustrates.quote: Answer Cues with Question Marks. Follow print when a question mark is shown standing alone representing a write-on-line. When print uses both a question mark and a low line or dash, ignore the question mark and use the underscore or dash. Insert a transcriber’s note explaining this usage.

print.printFeatures: A question mark is printed directly above a write-on-line underscore. The transcriber's note (print.transcriberNote) is braille-side text, not shown in the print.
print.transcriberNote: Print shows a question mark over an underscore. In braille, the question mark is omitted.

braille.notes: Independently re-extracted from source (fixed left margin / line-number field stripped by counting; U+2800→space; trailing spaces removed); confirmed byte-identical to both run A and run B (gold-10-A/gold-10-B) except where differences.md records a correction.

resolution: Braille matches both A and B exactly. Print unchanged from A/B; the TN wording is the given braille’s own note, back-translated. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.was: a 'note' block "Print shows a question mark over an underscore. In braille, the question mark is omitted." before the exercise; item text "What is \\_ right now?" (question mark dropped)
printCorrections.now: print.blocks holds the exercise item only, with the question mark kept: "What is \\_?\\_ right now?"; the note text is in print.transcriberNote
printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.262 (the file's pdfPages says 261; Example 10-22 is on the next page, printed 10-12), rendered at 110 dpi: the print original reads "What is _?_ right now?" with the question mark above the underline. The note is transcriber-written (10.6.10) and appears only in the braille lines; dropping the question mark from the item text was the transcriber's decision read off the braille.
